speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry will review the current liabilities and penalties under the Workplace Safety and Health Act; and (b) how can the Ministry further improve the workplace safety competency of companies and their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
text: These inspections resulted in companies taking remedial actions to rectify any safety gaps found in their worksites.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
text: The Council also has the bizSAFE and CultureSAFE initiatives for companies, which build WSH management capabilities and foster a stronger culture of WSH.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
text: We encourage members of the public to also play an active role to report any unsafe work practices by calling or emailing MOM or using our Snap@MOM mobile application to report any unsafe worksite practices.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The larger strategic direction taken by MOM is four-fold.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The second plank is to step up the training to build worker, management and line supervisors' capability on WSH.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The third is to continue with sustained enforcement actions and inspections at the different worksites.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Whenever there are areas identified to be of higher risk because of new situations, we will calibrate our enforcement regime to make sure that we will pay closer attention on those higher risk sectors.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: From time to time, we will assess the situation and needs.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: When it is meritorious, we will consider stiffening the penalties, which we have done in the last one year or so.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We think that it is important for the Government, the union and also the employers to come together to collectively tackle the WSH situation in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, collective ownership, tripartite ownership, is one area where we are looking into.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: And the second area of review is facilitating the public release of incident learning reports on the root causes and recommendations of incidents with higher learning value.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This is done so as to prevent recurrence of similar accidents.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This is still being evaluated and we will release more details when the review is finished by the end of this year.
